summary: Apple's framework is an app-side search hook: the system passes a captured camera or screenshot scene to an app, which returns matching content through App Intents. BifrOSt has no visual search and no scene-to-app delivery. Its App Intents, entity query and Core Spotlight code cover the App Intents half, which is only partly the same contract; the Apple Intelligence classification and Siri schemas have no counterpart.

features.feature: Visual search integration with the system camera and screenshots
features.apple: Visual Intelligence framework; Integrating your app with visual intelligence (article)
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 5 tests. Wave 2 (visual-intelligence, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No system pass of camera or screenshot content to apps and no app return path for matches. The camera has a QR scanner only. Checked 2026-10-17: the app-side return path (VisualSearchProvider and search, with app-id stamping) and the crop selection are in the code; the gap that remains is the system delivery of camera or screenshot scenes to the shell, which needs camera and screenshot capture on the device.

features.feature: SemanticContentDescriptor (scene labels, pixel buffer for apps)
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 8 tests. Wave 2 (visual-intelligence, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Scene labels come from Apple Intelligence classification, which is n/a. A BifrOSt version would need a local classifier and an app-facing type; neither exists.

features.feature: Adopting App Intents to support system experiences
features.apple: App Intents framework: AppIntent, AppEntity, EntityQuery, Spotlight and Shortcuts exposure
features.note: Typed intents, parameters, entity.query and [[intent]] manifest shortcuts that Spotlight lists are present. No Shortcuts app integration or Siri invocation; entity queries are served only over the control socket.

features.feature: Creating your first app intent (Spotlight and Shortcuts)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/intents.rs (Intent::new, shortcut, param, manifest_toml, validate); springboard/sdk/src/lib.rs (App::intents); springboard/src/shell/intents.rs (runnable, request_line)
features.note: A declared intent's manifest table, method name and parameter checks are tested in springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-tests-08.rs (first_intent). Spotlight lists shortcuts without parameters and runs them by calling intent.<id> on the app control socket; that shell side is not covered by these tests. A Shortcuts app does not exist in BifrOSt.

features.feature: Making actions and content discoverable by Apple Intelligence (schemas for Siri)
features.apple: App Intents schemas from relevant domains
features.note: Siri and Apple Intelligence are Apple services. BifrOSt has no schema registry and no assistant that consumes one.

features.feature: Content in system search results (Core Spotlight index, adjacent to Visual Intelligence results)
features.note: Apps index items; the Spotlight panel lists them under Documents and continue_activity opens them. Notes adopts it (springboard/apps/notes-desktop/src/main.rs). This is not Visual Intelligence, so it does not count toward the framework's status.

features.feature: Camera or screenshot object selection feeding a search
features.apple: Visual Intelligence camera search button; screenshot object selection
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 8 tests. Wave 2 (visual-intelligence, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The camera takes photos and reads QR codes. No object selection in screenshots and no search action on a frame.

gaps: No system delivery of camera or screenshot scenes to third-party apps (the core of the framework).

App return path is a model only: sdk visual_search::VisualSearchProvider answers a Scene with Matches, and search() stamps each match with the provider app id (tests in sdk/src/visual_search.rs); the shell does not call it yet.
Scene labels and pixels exist (ui visual_search::Scene::new, with_labels, pixel); the caller supplies the labels, nothing classifies the scene.
Object selection exists as Scene::crop(PixelRect) in ui visual_search; no screenshot UI feeds it yet.
App Intents are not exposed to a Shortcuts app or to a Siri-like assistant; entity queries are reachable only through the control socket and the Spotlight shortcut list.
